**Bottom line: on current information this resolves No.** The December 13 first round, which was one day before the deadline, has been called off indefinitely, and no new date has been set.

**What the resolution sources say (checked Oct 14, 2026)**
- **Wikipedia (2026 Haitian general election):** The version I retrieved still says general elections are scheduled to be held in Haiti on 13 December 2026. That looks out of date, since it doesn't reflect the Oct 6 postponement. It also notes runoffs on 21 February, with the final results to be announced on 7 March and a government inaugurated on 12 March 2027.
- **Metaculus FAQ:** I didn't open this page. As I understand it, "credible sources" generally means major news outlets and official bodies. Here that would include AFP, France 24, the Haitian Times and Haiti's electoral council (the CEP).

**Timeline**
- **Nov 2025 – Jan 2026:** The CEP first set Aug 30, 2026 for the first round. That date slipped. Authorities have repeatedly failed to meet electoral deadlines.
- **Feb 2026:** The transitional presidential council was dissolved in February 2026, leaving interim Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aime with sole executive authority.
- **July 20–28, 2026:** Voter registration began, and the CEP announced Dec 13 for the first round and Feb 21, 2027 for the runoff. It said the schedule would depend on an "acceptable security environment" and the availability of the financial resources.
- **Sept 23:** Seven presidential candidates had registered, and 628,755 voters were on the roll.
- **Oct 5:** The Council of Ministers adopted amendments to the June 2, 2026 electoral decree.
- **Oct 6–7:** The CEP postponed the campaign, which was due to start Oct 5, and moved the candidate registration deadline from Oct 9 to Oct 31. It gave no new election date, saying only the timetable "will be made public as soon as possible." A CEP member told AFP that "the December 13 date no longer stands", adding that "we are working on a new timetable". At that point only 769,000 voters had been registered since the process began on July 20.

**Status quo**
- No new date has been set. Registration is continuing, and the candidate filing deadline is now Oct 31.
- The original calendar had a 10-week campaign (Oct 5 to Dec 12). Even if a new calendar came out right away, there probably isn't enough time to vote before Dec 14.
- Gang violence, low voter registration, funding gaps and political disputes are still unresolved. Opponents have accused Fils-Aimé of trying to rig the vote.

**Base rate**
Haiti hasn't held a national election since 2016 and has repeatedly missed electoral deadlines since 2019. Earlier votes were also postponed, notably the 2015 runoff, which was delayed indefinitely and then re-run in 2016.

**Coming up before Dec 14**
- Oct 31: candidate and document deadline.
- A revised CEP calendar, expected but not yet dated.

**Prediction markets:** I didn't find any market prices.

criterios: This question resolves as **Yes** if, before December 14, 2026, according to [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) official popular voting begins in Haiti for the [2026 Haitian presidential election.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Haitian_general_election)
letra_pequena: Please note that non-presidential elections such as for the Senate or the Chamber of Deputies do not count.
razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** About two months. The outcome will be known by December 14, 2026.

(b) **Status quo:** No. The CEP postponed the elections indefinitely on Oct 6–7, and a CEP member said "the December 13 date no longer stands." No new date has been set, and the campaign hasn't started.

(c) **Reference class:** Haitian national elections after an indefinite postponement. Haiti hasn't held a national vote since 2016 and has missed every electoral deadline since 2019. Once Haiti slips a date, the vote is almost never brought forward or held within weeks. The base rate of voting within two months of an indefinite postponement is well under 5%.

(d) **No scenario:** The CEP publishes a new timetable placing the first round in 2027. Registration stays low, gang violence continues, funding gaps remain, and nothing happens before Dec 14. This is the most likely path.

(e) **Yes scenario:** The government reinstates Dec 13 or sets an earlier date, runs a shortened campaign after the Oct 31 candidate deadline, and opens voting before Dec 14. This would take a political push combined with sudden logistical and security readiness, which is very unlikely.

(f) **Technicalities:** Only official popular voting for the presidential election counts, and it must begin before Dec 14. Senate or Chamber votes don't count, and neither would mock or partial-registration exercises. Wikipedia still shows the old Dec 13 date, but that is a stale entry, not a resolution trigger. Only actual voting resolves Yes.

Probability: 2%

(a) **Time left:** About 61 days, until December 14, 2026. A Yes could become clear sooner if voting begins.

(b) **Status quo:** No. The electoral council has said the December 13 date no longer stands and has not announced a replacement.

(c) **Reference class:** Haitian national elections facing missed deadlines and security-related postponements. Haiti has not held a national election since 2016, and its recent electoral deadlines have repeatedly slipped. That points to a very low chance of holding this vote within the next two months, though the record is too small for a precise base rate.

(d) **No scenario:** The council issues a later timetable, or security and registration problems prevent voting before December 14.

(e) **Yes scenario:** Authorities rapidly set a new date and begin official presidential voting despite those obstacles.

(f) **Resolution technicality:** Voting need only **begin** before December 14. It need not finish, produce a result, or include legislative elections; legislative voting alone would not count.

Probability: 3%

(a) **Time left:** About 61 days until December 14, 2026.

(b) **Status quo:** No. The December 13 date has reportedly been withdrawn, and no replacement date has been announced.

(c) **Reference class:** Haiti’s proposed national-election timetables since its last national vote in 2016 have repeatedly slipped. That is a small, imperfect reference class, but its base rate for an on-time presidential vote is very low.

(d) **No scenario:** The electoral council publishes a new calendar for 2027 as registration and security problems persist.

(e) **Yes scenario:** Officials quickly restore a pre-deadline date, complete enough preparations, and begin presidential voting by December 13.

(f) **Resolution technicality:** Official *presidential* popular voting only needs to **begin** before December 14; it need not finish or produce results. Legislative voting alone would not count.
